channel.title: Bloomberg — diagnostic source feed
channel.description: Diagnostic feed grouped by acquisition connector.

item.title: CFPB Cuts May Leave Personal Financial Data at Risk, Report Says
item.description: US government databases containing sensitive financial information for millions of Americans may have been placed at risk after the Trump administration gutted the Consumer Financial Protection Bureau last year, according to a watchdog report.
item.dc:creator: J.J. McCorvey

item.title: OpenAI Parts Ways With 3 Workers Over Mishandling Information
item.description: OpenAI has parted ways with three employees for violating company policies on how private information should be handled, including for allegedly sharing it with an outside group.
item.dc:creator: Rachel Metz

item.title: Trump Memecoin Dinner Returns as Democrats Threaten Scrutiny
item.description: The promoter of Donald Trump’s memecoin is marketing another chance for top holders to attend an event with the president, just as Democratic lawmakers threaten fresh scrutiny of his crypto business dealings.
item.dc:creator: Olga Kharif

item.title: Factory and Cognition CEOs Feud Over ‘Unethical Conduct’ Claims
item.description: The head of artificial intelligence coding startup Factory is publicly feuding with the top executive at larger rival Cognition AI Inc. over allegations that a Factory adviser was involved in what he described as “unethical conduct” allegedly connected to Cognition.
item.dc:creator: Carmen Arroyo

item.title: How Vermillio Tackles AI's Creator Rights Challenge
item.description: As AI reshapes the entertainment industry, who controls and gets paid for the use of a creator's work and likeness? Vermillio is tackling that question with technology designed to track and license AI-generated content. Vermillio Co-Founder and CEO Dan Neely joins Ed Ludlow on "Bloomberg Tech." (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Luma AI Bets on ‘Hybrid’ Future for Hollywood
item.description: Luma AI COO Caroline Ingeborn says generative AI could help bring more film and television production back to Los Angeles by lowering costs and giving creators new ways to execute ambitious projects. She discusses why she sees AI as a tool for creative professionals rather than a replacement for them and how “hybrid filmmaking” can combine real actors and crews with AI-generated environments. She joins Ed Ludlow on "Bloomberg Tech." (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: AI Folks Don't Really Understand Intelligence Says Mukunda
item.description: A vast majority of Americans favor requiring artificial intelligence companies to meet independent safety benchmarks for their models, even if those standards mean slowing development of the technology, according to a new poll. Bloomberg Opinion Columnist and Lecturer at Yale School of Management Gautam Mukunda joins to discuss AI. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Promise CEO: AI Lets Smaller Teams Make Bigger Films
item.description: Promise CEO and Co-Founder George Strompolos is building what he calls an AI-native entertainment studio, using generative AI across development, production and visual effects. He says the technology can cut costs by more than 50% on some animated projects and allow smaller teams to create productions with far greater scale. He joins Ed Ludlow on "Bloomberg Tech." (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Bloomberg Tech Screentime Special
item.description: Bloomberg’s Ed Ludlow is live in LA for Bloomberg Screentime 2026, speaking with tech leaders and media entrepreneurs. Suno CEO Mikey Shulman discusses how AI is expanding — rather than simply disrupting — the music industry, Promise CEO George Strompolos and Luma AI COO Caroline Ingeborn talk about AI's growing role in filmmaking, and Vermillio CEO Dan Neely dives into the debate around AI and creators' rights. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Suno CEO: AI Could Reinvent How We Experience Music
item.description: Suno CEO and Co-Founder Mikey Shulman says AI could transform music from a largely passive experience into one where listeners actively create, remix and collaborate with their favorite artists. With more than 100 million users and partnerships across the music industry, Shulman discusses Suno’s in-house AI models, opportunities around licensing artists’ voices and music, and why he believes AI can expand the music business. He joins Ed Ludlow on "Bloomberg Tech." (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Google Faces $3.2 Billion Damage Claims on Ad-Tech Monopoly
item.description: USA Today Co., Daily Mail General and Trust Plc and a class of large publishers can seek more than $3.2 billion in damages for harm caused by monopolization of advertising technology markets by Alphabet Inc.’s Google, a New York federal judge ruled.
item.dc:creator: Leah Nylen and David Voreacos

item.title: Markets Face Rising Yields, AI Risks
item.description: Get a jump start on the US trading day with Dani Burger on "Bloomberg Open Interest." A new quarter begins with stocks battling a relentless rise in yields. Micron fuels the AI trade, Google rolls out Gemini 4 Argon, and Netflix plots its next act. Plus, Citi’s Kate Moore on why she's betting on stocks, Carlyle’s Mark Jenkins joins us to talk about hidden AI credit risks, and Aston Martin CEO Adrian Hallmark unveils the company's newest luxury SUV as it embarks on the road to a turnaround. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Apple’s Upcoming Smart Home Device Won’t Record Video
item.description: On this episode of the Power On podcast, Mark Gurman explains how Apple could pitch a video-free smart home camera with facial recognition as as an alternative to other smart home devices on the market. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Apple Wants to Take Over Your Home. Is Siri AI Ready?
item.description:
In the premiere episode of Power On, Mark Gurman and Bloomberg Tech Editor Vlad Savov discuss two of Apple’s most anticipated Fall releases. First, Mark shares his massive scoop on Apple’s long awaited push into the home and what makes their Siri AI-powered devices different from other smart home options. Then, Mark and Vlad consider if upgrading to the new iPhone 18 is worth it and question Apple’s reliance on influencer marketing.
Have a question for Mark? Email us at poweron@bloomberg.net or join the Power On Discord
Subscribe to the Power On Newsletter at https://www.bloomberg.com/poweron (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Carlyle Warns on AI Hype and Credit Risk Ahead
item.description: Amid the AI boom, private credit is pouring into data centers and hyperscalers, but the risks are real. Carlyle's Co-President Mark Jenkins joins Bloomberg Open Interest with a warning that concentration in a single hot theme can mirror the "SaaS apocalypse," where everything looked diversified until volatility hit. He breaks down where AI credit risk is building, how complex data‑center contracts can fail, and why old‑school diversification still matters more than AI hype. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Are We Losing Control of AI? What’s Driving New Fears
item.description: For years, as artificial intelligence has evolved from the stuff of sci-fi movies to an app ordinary people have installed on their phones, tech leaders and some AI insiders have talked about the potential for it to escape human control and wreak havoc on society. Those fears have become impossible to ignore in recent weeks, driven by advances in the technology, a series of cybersecurity breaches involving AI agents, and new warnings from rank-and-file AI staffers.
item.dc:creator: William Norris, Nilushi Karunaratne and Thomas Pfeiffer

item.title: Carney Invokes New Powers to Fast-Track Pacific Oil Pipeline
item.description: Prime Minister Mark Carney is expediting regulatory approval for a new, high-capacity oil pipeline to expand Canada’s access to Asian markets, with the aim of starting construction in September 2027.
item.dc:creator: Brian Platt

item.title: Carlyle Warns Private Credit AI Push Runs Concentration Risk
item.description: Private credit firms rushing to finance the artificial intelligence buildout risk encountering the same concentration problems that have plagued lenders exposed to software companies, according to Carlyle Group Inc.
item.dc:creator: Menghan Xiao and Scott Carpenter

item.title: Tesla Sell Ratings Slide as Street Says ‘Don’t Bet Against Musk’
item.description: Tesla Inc. shares have tumbled in 2026, but Wall Street analysts are increasingly reluctant to tell investors to sell.
item.dc:creator: Jordan Fitzgerald

item.title: SpaceX Launches Crew for NASA on Retiring Dragon Capsule
item.description: SpaceX launched a new crew of four astronauts to the International Space Station on Thursday, as questions swirl over the company’s plans for the future of its human spaceflight program.
item.dc:creator: Loren Grush
